title: Polymer coordination enables alloying-free synthesis of stable α-FAPbI3 thick films for real-time X-ray imaging
source: Matter
abstract: Stable α-FAPbI3 is promising for high-performance X-ray imaging but is difficult to produce without alloying. Here, polymer coordination with PVP enables stable, alloying-free α-FAPbI3 thick films by controlling crystallization and lattice strain. The resulting detectors combine high sensitivity, low-dose operation, and fast response, enabling high-resolution, real-time X-ray imaging.

title: Regulating carrier transport and oxychloride interphase formation by increasing configurational complexity in solid-state halide electrolytes
source: Joule
abstract: Cost-effective Li2ZrCl6 halides with regulated configurational complexity combine rapid lithium-ion conduction with ultralow electronic conductivity and superior oxidative stability. A robust zirconium oxychloride cathode-electrolyte interphase is formed during cycling, enabling 4.4 V all-solid-state LiNi0.85Co0.1Mn0.05O2 batteries to operate for up to 3,700 cycles.

title: Programmable mRNA vaccine materials for temporal control of antitumour immunity
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: Advances in mRNA and nanomaterial design have transformed vaccine technology, enabling precise control of antigen expression, delivery kinetics and immune activation. However, several leading clinical-stage mRNA cancer vaccine programmes are being evaluated in the adjuvant setting, in which loss of the primary tumour antigen reservoir and evolving postoperative immune states may alter the conditions for effective priming. Here, we present a materials-driven framework for temporal immunoengineering, in which programmable mRNA vaccine materials are designed to align antigen availability, innate sensing and adaptive priming with changing immune states across the perioperative window. Using the perioperative period as an illustrative model of immune flux, we discuss how distinct mRNA nanocarrier architectures can be engineered to tune the timing, magnitude and anatomical context of innate activation, antigen expression and adaptive priming. A universal neoadjuvant mRNA ‘prime’, formulated in an immunostimulatory nanocarrier, could condition innate and myeloid compartments and remodel the tumour microenvironment, whereas a personalized adjuvant ‘boost’, delivered in translationally efficient formulations, could reinforce clonal expansion and memory of tumour-specific T cells. By treating biomaterials as programmable regulators of immunodynamics rather than passive carriers, this Perspective establishes temporal control as a complementary design axis for next-generation mRNA vaccine systems.

title: Decoding the risks of hydrogels for bone regeneration
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: Engineered hydrogels provide hydrated, tunable and biointeractive matrices for bone regeneration, but few have advanced from preclinical promise to defined clinical indications. This translational gap reflects application-specific failure in dynamic bone microenvironments rather than a lack of material innovation alone. In this Review, we decode hydrogel risks across craniofacial filling, long-bone reconstruction, osteochondral repair, local drug delivery, cell delivery, implant coating and oral modulation of metabolic bone disease. We organize these failures into mechanical gap, spatiotemporal mismatch and immune dysregulation and further identify emerging long-term and systemic risks. Finally, we position experimental hydrogels against clinical products, manufacturability constraints and large-animal benchmarks to propose risk-controlled design principles for next-generation bone-regenerative hydrogels.

title: Ultrastable 4.99 V Li rich Mn-based cathodes achieved by catalytic-shielded and strain-buffered interface engineering
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxides (LROs) offer high theoretical capacity but are limited by irreversible oxygen redox, voltage fade, and structural degradation upon cycling. Herein, we develop a dual-interface engineering strategy for LRO cathodes, integrating a catalytic-shielded carbon coating and interface-confined discrete spinel domains. The carbon layer decouples electrolyte decomposition from lattice-driven catalysis, suppressing cathode-electrolyte interphase growth and oxygen release, while subsurface-confined spinel phases establish three-dimensional Li+ transport pathways and mitigate lattice strain. Ex-situ hard/soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy confirm enhanced anionic redox reversibility and stable charge compensation. Consequently, the optimized LRO achieves an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.1% with a discharge capacity of 295 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C, compared with 267 mAh g−1 and 79.0% for the pristine counterpart. It maintains 88.9% capacity after 150 cycles at 4.99 V (vs. 29.4% for pristine after 80 cycles) and 79.2% after 200 cycles at 45°C. Remarkably, a 1.58 Ah Si/C||HV-LRO pouch cell delivers 307 Wh kg−1 energy density and retains 70.7% capacity after 100 cycles at 0.8 C, demonstrating practical viability for high-energy applications. This work establishes a paradigm for stabilizing high-voltage LRO cathodes through spatially decoupled interfacial catalysis and reinforcement.

title: Enzymatic oxidative esterification with an unconventional regioselective control
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Esters have widespread applications in nature and industry, making the strategic installation of ester bonds critical for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, polymers and other functional materials. However, achieving regioselective esterification of sterically demanding secondary alcohols in the presence of more reactive primary sites remains a formidable challenge. Here we report the engineering of aldehyde dehydrogenases into oxidative ester synthases (OxiEs) with divergent selectivities. Structure-guided protein engineering yielded two complementary catalyst classes: imidazole-dependent OxiEs1 favours primary alcohols and imidazole-independent OxiEs2 exhibits exclusive selectivity for secondary alcohols. Mechanistic studies revealed that imidazole acts as a molecular switch, allosterically tuning the active-site geometry to control regioselectivity. This system demonstrates a broad substrate scope, enabling direct, highly selective acylation of various secondary alcohols. Furthermore, we showcase its utility in controlling enantioselectivity, enabling redox-neutral synthesis and preparing valuable esters on gram-scale. This work establishes a strategy for regioselective control in esterification, transforming a classical hydride-transfer enzyme into a tunable platform for ester bond formation under mild, sustainable conditions.

title: Non-equilibrium fluctuations in the corrosion process
source: Matter
abstract: Why does corrosion attack specific sites under some conditions but spread uniformly under others? Liang et al. combine real-time nanoscale imaging with atomistic simulations to show that corrosion reflects a competition between local structural heterogeneity and thermodynamic driving force. Near equilibrium, strained regions preferentially corrode and promote localized pitting; far from equilibrium, stronger driving forces overwhelm these local differences and produce rapid, uniform corrosion. The findings provide a framework for understanding and controlling localized material degradation.

title: PFAS flows, treatment and reduction in data centre infrastructure
source: Nature Reviews Clean Technology
abstract: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are used and emitted across data centre infrastructure, including semiconductor manufacturing, data centre cooling and end-of-life management. The accelerating deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) amplifies these existing challenges by increasing infrastructure demand, cooling intensity and hardware turnover. In this Review, we identify PFAS use and release points across data centre infrastructure and describe strategies for their capture, destruction, reduction and substitution. PFAS management priorities include developing process-compatible substitutes for semiconductor manufacturing, balancing thermal performance and safety in PFAS-free cooling and controlling releases from residual coolants and PFAS-containing components during disposal and recycling. Treatment varies with PFAS concentration and physical form. Options include activated carbon adsorption and ion exchange for wastewater, high-temperature incineration for concentrated liquid and solid wastes, and thermal or catalytic oxidation for gaseous streams. Implementation of these treatment and substitution strategies is constrained by the availability of validated alternatives, treatment scalability and gaps in PFAS flow data. Expanding use restrictions and application-specific exemptions shape substitution timelines, and downstream release limits and reporting requirements demand continued emission control and supply-chain transparency. Improvements in computing efficiency, cascaded reuse of AI hardware and PFAS phase-out roadmaps in data centre infrastructure could enable long-term, source-level PFAS reduction.

title: 16.52% Efficiency All‐Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells via Al‐Doped ZnO/SnO2 Electron Transport Bilayer for Improved Interfacial Energy‐Level Alignment
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:

AZO‐based devices substantially outperform ZnO‐based controls, delivering a PCE of 16.52% versus 15.21%, with suppressed dark current, reduced trap density, lower non‐radiative recombination, and smaller hysteresis. The AZO device retains 80% of its initial efficiency after 662 h of continuous illumination, compared with only 312 h for the ZnO counterpart. Al

title: Trash to Treasure: PFAS‐Functionalized MOFs for Boosted Piezocatalytic H2 Production
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) hold broad prospects in piezocatalysis because of their high surface area, porosity, and tunable structures, yet pristine MOFs frequently suffer from poor piezocatalytic response. Herein, this study pioneers a novel strategy using pollutant perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) as a functional additive to post‐synthetically modify MOF‐808(Hf), fabricating MOF‐808(Hf)‐F for piezocatalytic hydrogen production. PFHxA modification remarkably enhances the polarity of MOF‐808(Hf) (dipole moment from 8.90 to 12.58 D) and piezoelectricity (d

In addition, MOF‐808(Hf) achieves a PFHxA removal efficiency of approximately 40.1% from water. This work realizes simultaneous per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) removal and efficient energy production, with excellent universality for Hf‐based MOFs with unsaturated metal sites.

title: Helical Keratin‐Derived Aqueous Binders for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) possess ultrahigh energy density, low cost, and environmental friendliness, making them strong contenders for next‐generation energy storage technologies. However, their development is hindered by multiple interfacial challenges, including the shuttling of lithium polysulfides (LiPS), sluggish reaction kinetics, and severe volume expansion of the cathode. To address these issues, a multifunctional biomass‐derived aqueous binder was designed by crosslinking an α‐helical protein (α‐HP) with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and glycerol (GL). The α ‐helical structure of α‐HP in the α‐HP/PVA/GL adhesive acts as a “molecular spring”, effectively buffering volume expansion and stabilizing the electrode structure. Additionally, its abundant N‐ and O‐containing polar groups efficiently anchor LiPS, significantly suppressing the shuttling effect and accelerating redox kinetics. Consequently, lithium‐sulfur batteries employing the α‐HP/PVA/GL binder exhibit exceptional long‐term cycling stability. The α‐HP/PVA/GL cathode delivers an initial discharge specific capacity of 737.3 mAh g
                    −1
                    and retains 487.9 mAh g
                    −1
                    after 600 stable cycles at 2 C, with an average capacity decay rate of only 0.056% per cycle. This study provides a green, facile, and efficient strategy for developing multifunctional binders to overcome practical bottlenecks in lithium‐sulfur battery applications.

title: Engineering Thermoelectric‐Electrocatalytic Coupling in RuO2/PrCoO3 Heterointerface for Efficient Oxygen Evolution
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is pivotal for diverse electrochemical energy conversion systems; however, it has so far been plagued by sluggish kinetics and excessive energy consumption. In this study, we proposed an innovative thermoelectric‐electrocatalytic coupling strategy to enhance OER efficiency by constructing an Ohmic heterointerface through uniform integration of RuO
                    2
                    with thermoelectric oxide (PrCoO
                    3
                    ). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses revealed that the thermoelectric potential generated by PrCoO
                    3

                    2

                    2
                    /PrCoO
                    3
                    heterointerface delivered exceptional OER performance under a mild temperature gradient (Δ
                    T

                    −2
                    from 300 mV (Δ
                    T
                    = 0°C) to 178 mV, 4 300% increase in current density, and negligible potential loss over 1,000 h. When the catalyst was assembled into an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the cell driven by spontaneous heating reached a low voltage of 2.18 V at a current density of 2.0 A cm

title: Anti‐Poisoning Tin Single‐Atom Unlocks High‐Activity Ruthenium Catalysts for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The practical deployment of anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) is constrained by the lack of efficient electrocatalysts for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), primarily due tothe sluggishVolmer step and inefficient intermediate desorption. While Ru‐based catalysts exhibit promising *H binding energy, their practical performance is compromised by poor water dissociation kinetics and susceptibility to active‐site blockage by adsorbed species. Herein, we report a Sn‐doped RuO
                    2
                    @Ru catalyst supported on carbon black, wherein atomically dispersed Sn modulates the electronic structure of RuO
                    2
                    via Sn─O bonds, simultaneously facilitating water dissociation, optimizing *H adsorption, and preventing *OH poisoning. The catalyst achieves exceptional performance with an overpotential of 9 mV at 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    , positioning it among the most active HER catalysts reported to date. When integrated into a full AEMWE, it operates at 1.85 V and 1000 mA cm
                    −2
                    with stability exceeding 300 h. Mechanistic studies suggest that Sn doping fine‐tunes the *OH and *H binding energies, addressing the kinetic imbalance inherent in conventional Ru catalysts. This work highlights the effectiveness of atomic‐level electronic engineering via an anti‐poisoning strategy for designing efficient, stable alkaline HER electrocatalysts toward industrial hydrogen production.

title: Predicting birth weights in West Africa using subseasonal to seasonal climate and socioeconomic variables shows potential for an early warning system
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Past research has shown a negative impact of climate extremes on child birth weight (BW), which is modulated by household socioeconomic and individual maternal conditions as well as the timing and degree of exposure. This study tests the potential of predicting BW using subseasonal to seasonal (S2S) climate predictors and socioeconomic indicators to support early warning systems for BW. Three sets of predictors were tested: a) a suite of biological and socioeconomic indicators from the Demographic and Health Survey (DHS), b) S2S climate predictors, and c) a combination of climate predictors and selected socioeconomic indicators. The most accurate models incorporated the full set of DHS variables [predictors set (a)], with within-country (models trained and tested on the same country) predictive errors ranging from 13.5 to 17% for Burkina Faso and 20 to 25% for Mali. Cross-country (models trained on one country and tested on others) errors varied from 14 to 21% in Burkina Faso to 20 to 26% in Senegal. Models using only climate predictors [predictors set (b)] showed comparable skill to those using the full set of DHS indicators, with a relative error difference of 1 to 5%. The predictive skill was highest for children born with the most in-utero exposure to the lean season (months between planting and harvest). The results of this study have important implications for the prospect of implementing child BW early warning systems in data-sparse regions, based solely on climate predictors or based on selected socioeconomic indicators with climate predictors, to support malnutrition surveillance, to improve antenatal/maternal nutrition, policy formulation, and mitigation decisions.

title: In vitro binding energies capture Klf4 occupancy across the human genome
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Transcription factors (TFs) regulate gene expression by binding to specific genomic loci determined by DNA sequence. Their sequence specificity is commonly summarized by a consensus binding motif. However, eukaryotic genomes contain billions of low-affinity DNA sequences to which TFs associate with a sequence-dependent binding energy. We currently lack insight into how the genomic sequence defines this spectrum of binding energies and the resulting pattern of TF localization. Here, we set out to obtain a quantitative understanding of sequence-dependent TF binding to both motif and nonmotif sequences. We achieve this by first pursuing accurate measurements of physical binding energies of human TF Krüppel-like factor 4 (Klf4) to a library of short DNA sequences in a fluorescence-anisotropy-based bulk competitive binding assay. Second, we show that the highly nonlinear sequence dependence of Klf4 binding energies can be captured by combining a linear model of binding energies with an Ising model of the coupled recognition of nucleotides by a TF. title: Equity dimensions of future vulnerabilities to climate hazards: Long-term spatial population projections for New York City consistent with Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Projections of future population are important for a myriad of reasons. Large cities, states, and countries routinely produce near- and mid-range population projections. In the context of climate change, the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) framework is used at global and national scales to project long-term population to inform future emissions scenarios and understand future climate-related exposures and impacts. Much less consideration has been given to long-term projections at smaller scales, even though climate impacts are place based and cities now host most of the world’s population. Cities and their metropolitan regions are complex, heterogeneous in terms of population, environmental, and built features. Thus, using global or national-scale approaches overlooks important aspects of urban futures. Cities are diverse, fluid population centers home to migrants, with employment opportunities yet substantial inequality. These quintessential city-centric features are ignored in global/national-scale population projection methods, including long-term ones consistent with the SSPs. Leveraging state-level SSP-based projections, here we extend that approach for New York City, currently home to 8.8 million persons. Combining multistate and multiregional demographic projection and spatial downscaling models, we project county-level population by racial/ethnic groups and age–sex to 2100 and downscale to 100 m. Such projections allow for an equity lens to inform assessments of future vulnerabilities to climate hazards. Four of the five SSPs project that the population of New York City will be smaller and much older at the end of the century, though these futures are dependent on demographic assumptions about fertility and especially migration.

title: Sources and sinks: Geoclimatic dynamics shaped the assembly of endemic fauna in the world’s Third Pole
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP), a biodiversity hotspot shaped by tectonic and climatic forces, has seen significant progress in understanding its floristic origins. However, a comprehensive, multitaxon perspective on how its terrestrial fauna assembled remains lacking. Here we integrate time-calibrated phylogenies of over 20,000 species from five major groups (invertebrates, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals), to reconstruct the evolutionary history of 527 terrestrial animal species endemic to the QTP. Our finding reveals that the QTP has functioned both as a center of in situ diversification and as a “biogeographic sink” that receives species from surrounding regions, however, with pronounced subregional differentiation: the Hengduan Mountains acted primarily as a diversification source, while the Himalaya and the Plateau Platform acted as sinks, accumulating lineages from adjacent regions. The Eocene–Oligocene climatic transition, rather than late Neogene uplift, initiated sustained faunal diversification and biotic exchange. Across subregions, distinct uplift histories and monsoon regimes drove asynchronous evolutionary trajectories, showing that even geographically adjacent regions can exhibit distinct accumulation patterns of lineages. Notably, integrating our faunal evidence with recent floristic assembly data reveals a consistent “plants first, animals later” pattern across the QTP and its subregions, suggesting that early-arriving plant lineages created ecological niches that facilitated subsequent faunal colonization and diversification. This framework advances our understanding of how mountain biotas assemble over time, with implications extending far beyond the QTP.
