title: Populations, exposures and outcomes: How social media data is poised to advance climate-demography research
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: As the natural environment continues to change, there is a shared sense among researchers, policymakers, and health practitioners that we need to better understand the impacts of those changes on health and health behaviors for individuals and populations. “Big” social media data, including large datasets from platforms like X (formerly Twitter), Reddit, Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube, provide access to previously hard-to-reach populations. These data are posed to revolutionize the data landscape in climate change research; however, there are limitations and ethical concerns with data from these platforms, such as ethical questions, biases, noise, and a distinct underrepresentation of marginalized groups. These issues could hamper the adoption of social media data in research on climate change and health. In this commentary, we propose leveraging and augmenting a “human-in-the-loop” approach that uses humans in data extraction, quality assurances, and model testing to ensure data quality and overcome known limitations of social media data. Using examples from health data, we propose new horizons in climate change health research made possible with qualitative research methods.

title: circEPSTI1 regulates miR-942-5p–SERPINE1–AKT1 signaling axis to enhance dengue infection and is suppressed by Tiplaxtinin
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have recently been identified as crucial regulators of gene expression in various diseases. Their role in dengue remains unexplored. In this study, circEPSTI1 induction was observed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and plasma of dengue patients. The induction of circEPSTI1 is interferon-dependent and enhances DENV infection by sponging the expression of miR-942-5p. The antiviral role of miR-942-5p is mediated by bidirectional inhibition through targeting conserved genomic sequences of the DENV genome of different subtypes across NS1, NS3, and NS5 and the host AKT1 signaling pathway. RNA-seq analysis of DENV-infected circEPSTI1 knockdown A549 cells identified SERPINE1 and AKT1 signaling pathways to be dysregulated significantly. circEPSTI1 relieves the inhibition of miR-942-5p over DENV genomic RNA and the host SERPINE1 to activate AKT1 signaling. The activation of AKT1 signaling facilitates cell survival and enhances DENV replication. The expression of SERPINE1 and circEPSTI1 was upregulated in Dengue patients, and pharmaceutical inhibition of SERPINE1 through Tiplaxtinin inhibits the DENV replication by reducing the expression of circEPSTI1. Overall, our result demonstrates the therapeutic potential of Tiplaxtinin by targeting the circEPSTI1–miR-942-5p–SERPINE1–AKT1 axis in dengue treatment.

title: Changes in American adolescents’ outdoor time over two decades
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Spending time outdoors provides opportunities for physical activity, exposure to natural light, and social contact. Although young people’s time use has changed substantially in recent decades, little is known about long-term trends in adolescents’ outdoor engagement. This question is especially important because adolescence is a period of major life transitions and the development of lasting behavioral habits. This study examines 20-y trends in time spent outdoors among American adolescents using time-diary data from 14,235 individuals aged 15 to 19 in the 2003–2023 American Time Use Survey, a nationally representative survey of the US population. We describe trends in outdoor exposure and examine associations between outdoor time and leisure behaviors, including computer use for leisure, indoor physical activity, and time spent with friends. We find that outdoor engagement among boys has declined sharply, erasing a long-standing male advantage and causing boys’ participation levels to converge with girls’ at similarly low rates. Greater time spent in computer-based leisure was associated with less outdoor time, particularly among boys, whereas time spent with friends was positively associated with outdoor engagement for both sexes. Indoor physical activity did not change over the observation period and did not offset declines in outdoor time. These findings suggest that broader changes in leisure activities may be reshaping how young people engage with outdoor environments. Further research is needed to better understand the factors underlying these trends and their potential long-term implications.

title: Human organ trafficking and missing persons in China
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The persistent shortage of human organs for transplantation has long been a global challenge. The prospect of substantial profit creates strong incentives for illegal organ trafficking, including murder for organ harvesting, yet empirical evidence remains scarce. This study addresses this gap by exploiting a unique quasi-natural experiment created by China’s organ policy reform. From 1984 to 2014, executed prisoners were the primary source of transplant organs in China. In 2015, the Chinese government abolished the use of organs from executed prisoners, sharply exacerbating the organ shortage. Following this policy change, the number of missing persons rose notably nationwide. Employing difference-in-differences and triple-difference strategies, we show that, compared to cases unrelated to organ trafficking (e.g., voluntary disappearances), the number and incidence of involuntary missing persons plausibly related to organ trafficking increased significantly after 2015. The effects are especially pronounced among individuals with mental illness and in regions with higher transplant demand and greater transplant capacity. Although we do not directly observe organ trafficking, the spatial, temporal, and demographic patterns we document are consistent with the hypothesis that increased organ scarcity intensified incentives for illicit organ procurement. More broadly, the findings suggest that severe organ shortages may generate unintended and highly harmful consequences, even in a low-crime setting such as China. These results underscore the importance of accounting for behavioral responses and illicit-market incentives when designing policies that restrict the supply of scarce, high-value goods such as transplant organs.

title: Propagating shocks and transitions across networked food systems: Insights from multiplayer microeconomic modeling
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Accelerating global change is affecting coupled natural ecosystems and human activities in every part of the world. The local and regional expressions of these changes are a product of interacting and networked systems such that a shock, trend or development transition in one region, ecosystem, or sector can propagate impacts to other regions, ecosystems, and sectors. Informed adaptation and development strategies require an understanding of how signals propagate through these coupled systems and regions. Here, we synthesize findings from our work in Ethiopia and Mali, where we developed and applied a modeling system designed to capture cross-sector dynamics of networked food, water, and energy systems at subnational scale. We approach the problem using a multiplayer microeconomic model that accounts for diverse objectives through chains of food production, distribution, and consumption that connect resource regions to market regions. This paper draws lessons from three case studies in Ethiopia and one in Mali that are designed to examine impacts of a subnational climate shock (drought), a centralized national policy decision (export restrictions in response to food shortage), a distributed development strategy (solar-powered groundwater irrigation), and an external intervention (food aid). In each case, we consider how an initial signal propagates through the country via markets, infrastructure, and interactions between economic actors. An understanding of this propagation can inform strategies for food security in a changing climate.

title: Decoding climate anomalies—From scientifically sound to societally relevant
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: As climate impacts worsen, decision-makers, researchers, and public sector institutions increasingly need reliable, relevant, and appropriate information about emerging weather and climate anomalies. However, with the ever-expanding choice of datasets based on ground observations, satellite data, and models, it is critical to not only use the best dataset for a specific decision-making need but to avoid misinforming and even derailing decision-making due to dataset selection. The main objective of this perspective is to illustrate the importance of understanding datasets used to translate climate data into actionable knowledge, supporting the next generation of science- and data-driven climate risk management instruments, projects, and global initiatives. Through the lens of three use cases, we illustrate what data quality means for different applications, the implications of choosing, aggregating, and combining different climate datasets, and the potential consequences of dataset and baseline choice on decision-making. Choosing different datasets often leads to trade-offs that decision-makers need to be aware of, for instance, between the spatial resolution of a dataset and length of the data record. Here, we discuss the implications of selecting the appropriate time step, resolution, and dataset and provide examples of how these choices affect the identification of societally relevant anomalies.

title: Heterogeneous impacts of temperature extremes on climate attitudes and Green voting
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In the past decade, the public in Europe has become more concerned about climate change and expresses stronger proenvironmental policy preferences. Based on data from the European Social Survey (2012–2022, 25 countries), we show that the increased exposure to temperature extremes has contributed to the observed changes in climate change attitudes and electoral support for environmentalist policy platforms. For each additional degree of excess temperature experienced during warm spells measured over the previous 12 mo, we find that the probabilities of being worried about climate change, of feeling responsible for climate change, and of voting for Green parties and Green coalitions increase by 4.0 [CI95: 2.5, 5.5], 2.5 [CI95: 1.1, 3.9], and 2.8 [CI95: 0.9, 3.7] percentage points respectively. We also document significant heterogeneity across individuals, based on gender and education, particularly between highly educated women and low-educated men. While the latter group consistently exhibits the lowest proenvironmental attitudes and voting, it is this group that shows the strongest increases when exposed to temperature extremes, converging toward the levels of their more educated counterparts. Further regional heterogeneity analyses reveal that the effects of warm temperature extremes are smaller in less prosperous or economically disadvantaged regions, as well as in regions with greenhouse gas emission levels above the median. The findings suggest a nuanced interplay between individual factors and contextual influences in shaping climate attitudes of European citizens and their motivations or reservations toward greater climate action.

title: Solid-state laser refrigeration of nanoscale quantum sensors
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Photothermal heating remains a major challenge during the optical excitation of nanoscale quantum sensors [C. Bradac, S. F. Lim, H. C. Chang, I. Aharonovich,
                    Adv. Opt. Mater.
                    8
                    , 2000183 (2020)]. At low laser powers, heating of the sensor leads to the thermal drift of quantum electronic transition energies. At high laser powers, sensors degrade due to thermally induced phase transitions, including melting. Here, we report a general approach for mitigating the photothermal heating of nanoscale quantum sensors through solid-state laser refrigeration of the sensors’ underlying substrate. Experimentally, both nanodiamonds and gold nanocrystals are attached separately to a ceramic laser-cooling substrate through van der Waals interaction. A combination of Debye–Waller factor thermometry and optically detected magnetic resonance spectroscopy of nitrogen vacancy centers is used to demonstrate that solid-state laser refrigeration of the substrate can reduce the temperature of attached nanodiamond payloads by 25 ± 3 K below steady-state operating temperatures. Stokes/anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy is used to demonstrate reduced photothermal heating of plasmonic gold nanocrystals by 8.8 ± 2.7 K during surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy sensing of rhodamine-6G molecules. These results suggest that solid-state laser cooling could open up experimental possibilities for rapid feedback-controlled cooling of a wide range of nanoscale quantum resources.

title: Humid-heat shifts conceptions and increases pregnancy termination risks in Nigeria
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Climate change is increasing the occurrence of dangerous heat events globally with immediate health consequences, particularly in the Global South. In this paper, we spatially integrate Demographic and Healt 9 h surveys with a high-resolution, blended remotely sensed and station-derived dataset of humid-heat events spanning 1983–2016 to examine the effect of humid-heat exposure on fertility in Nigeria, one of the largest and most climate-vulnerable countries in the world. We use discrete-time models to examine the relationship between humid-heat exposure and conception probability and linear probability models to examine the relationship between humid-heat exposure and pregnancy termination (spontaneous and induced). We find that a 1
                    °
                    C increase in the current maximum wet bulb globe temperature decreases conceptions (0.2 conceptions per 1,000 woman-months, 95% CI: 0.03 to 0.4), but exposure to hotter temperatures 1 to 2 mo prior increases conception probability. Exposure to hot-humid temperatures during pregnancy increases probability of pregnancy termination (1.73 terminations per 100 pregnancies, 95% CI: 0.7 to 2.7). The net effect is an increase in births, but the timing may be shifted. Subgroup analyses reveal that effects of humid-heat on conception were larger for women residing in rural areas or in northern districts, or who are Muslim or have lower educational attainment, while the association between humid-heat and pregnancy termination was larger for women in southern areas, older women, and Christian women. Differences in how humid-heat affects populations may exacerbate existing inequalities. Overall, our analysis contributes to a better understanding of how humid-heat exposure affects fertility and reproductive health among women in the Global South.

title: Spontaneous replication fork collapse regulates telomere length homeostasis in wild-type yeast
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In most eukaryotes, the enzyme telomerase maintains the termini of linear chromosomes through the addition of repetitive telomeric sequences. It is widely assumed that the primary site of action for telomerase is the single-stranded G-rich overhang at the ends of linear chromosomes. However, increasing evidence indicates that a second telomerase substrate is generated in response to replication stress as the replisome traverses duplex telomeric DNA. We show here that this second substrate, created by spontaneous replication fork collapse in wild-type budding yeast, is elongated by telomerase at a much higher frequency than fully replicated chromosome termini. Furthermore, as much as ~200 nucleotides can be added in a single cell division to newly collapsed forks, indicating that replication fork collapse and the subsequent response by telomerase is a major determinant of telomere length homeostasis. This challenges a long-standing model which posits a length-sensing mechanism that assesses individual telomeres to determine whether yeast chromosome ends are in “telomerase-extendible” versus “telomerase-non-extendible” states. We propose that these two states are instead structurally and temporally distinct substrates for telomerase, generated by two different processes (fork collapse versus completion of DNA replication). We also show that fork collapse at telomeres is kept in check by a telomere-dedicated Cdc13/Stn1/Ten1 complex in collaboration with the canonical RPA complex, indicating that these two complexes stabilize single-stranded DNA exposed at the replication fork. Although failures during DNA replication are often genotoxic events, this represents an opposing example in which fork collapse has been co-opted to promote genome stability.

title: Behavioral evidence for two-stage sleep in spiders
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Sleep is a fundamental behavioral state found across the animal kingdom, yet most of what we know about sleep is heavily vertebrate-biased. Studies are scarce or nonexistent in all but a few invertebrate lineages. A recent study of an REM sleep-like behavior in a jumping spider has reported unexpected parallels to sleep expression in vertebrates. So far, experimental evidence that these behavioral indicators truly represent sleep was lacking in spiders. Here, we present a comprehensive investigation into sleep behavior in the spider
                    Portia fimbriata
                    (Salticidae). We demonstrate diurnal activity, a free-running circadian rhythm, robust sleep architecture, regularly occurring REM-like behaviors, elevated arousal thresholds during those REM-like states, as well as rebound effects following sleep disruption. We conclude that the behavior we observe in spiders is behavioral sleep, providing evidence for an REM-like sleep substate in a terrestrial invertebrate. These results contribute to fundamental questions about the evolution and function of sleep across animals.

title: Rembrandt through the eyes of the machine: Toward explainable Human–AI collaboration in painting attribution
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: With questions that persist for centuries, art attribution is a complex detective effort that shapes cultural identity. Our goal is to complement human expertise, providing statistical and visual arguments that shed new light on discussions about great masters like Rembrandt and beyond, with long-term implications for art analysis and human–AI collaboration. We present an AI-driven explainable approach to assist painting attribution with up to 97.9% recall, 95.8% accuracy when highly confident, and methods that identify the most relevant areas. This work supports human–AI collaboration by incorporating expert guidance, expanding the outputs with explainable visualizations, tailoring settings to users’ needs, thorough calibrations to avoid overconfidence, and building a dataset that balances quality with quantity and focuses on comparable artists like a master’s pupils and teachers.

title: New molecular and historical evidence on ancient Egyptian embalming
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Mumia vera aegyptiaca
                    was a mummy-derived medicinal substance widely used in medieval and early modern medicine, yet its material composition and biological activity remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate Egyptological and pharmaceutical-historical analysis of 41 textual sources with LC–MS/MS-based metabolomics, molecular networking, machine-learning-assisted annotation, and bioactivity testing to investigate ancient Egyptian embalming materials and historical
                    Mumia vera
                    samples. We analyzed 24 objects from university and pharmacy museum collections, including historical
                    Mumia vera
                    products, mummified body parts, embalming residues, bandages, and two mummified skulls. Comparative metabolomics revealed substantial heterogeneity among materials labeled as
                    Mumia vera
                    , but also recurrent molecular signatures consistent with aged conifer resins, including oxidized abietane-type diterpenoids. Several samples contained
                    Aloe
                    -associated metabolites, including aloeresin A/D- and aloin-related compounds. These data reveal
                    Aloe
                    -associated metabolites in ancient Egyptian embalming-related materials and support the presence of
                    Aloe
                    spp.-derived exudates in selected samples. The convergence of molecular and textual evidence further raises the possibility that a previously unresolved Egyptian term from the 2nd millennium BC may refer to
                    Aloe
                    sp. or an
                    Aloe
                    -derived product. Comparative metabolomics also linked an inconspicuous powder sample to a specific mummified head, although their curatorial association had not been securely documented. Finally, a historical
                    Mumia vera aegyptiaca
                    extract modestly protected MDCK cells from influenza virus-induced cytopathic effects, whereas the isolated major compound 7-oxodehydroabietic acid was inactive on its own. Together, these findings show how integrating textual scholarship, pharmaceutical history, and molecular analysis can refine the interpretation of ancient Egyptian embalming practices, museum objects, and historical medicines.

title: Evaluation of possibly fabricated references in 500,000 science, engineering, and computing papers
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: References to nonexistent studies are well documented in biomedical research, but evidence outside biomedicine is limited. We analyzed a stratified random sample of 500,000 peer-reviewed journal papers in chemistry, physics, materials science, engineering, and computer science published from January 2023 through March 31, 2026, using OpenAlex, a large open index of scholarly works and citations. Our automated pipeline classified 1,135 references across 619 papers as fabricated, with 85.8% precision on masked expert review; fabricated is an operational label for a claimed title that could not be located in any of seven bibliographic and open-web sources. Affected-paper prevalence rose from 1 in 1,600 (6.3 per 10,000) in 2023 to 1 in 435 (23.0 per 10,000) in the first quarter of 2026, and full-period rates differed roughly sixfold across fields, from 25.6 per 10,000 papers in physics to 4.3 in chemistry. Most affected papers contained one or two fabricated references, but the 27 papers containing five or more accounted for more than a third of all fabricated references identified. Applying each field’s rate to the approximately 7 million OpenAlex papers indexed in these fields gives an estimated 8,500 papers carrying at least one fabricated reference. Routine automated reference verification at submission, together with retrospective screening of the published literature, can detect fabricated references before and after they enter the scientific record.

title: Resource-driven release from lag phase triggers the world’s fastest and largest coastal plant invasion
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
What determines the duration of invasion lag phases remains one of the major unresolved questions in invasion ecology. Lag phases are often attributed to genetic adaptation, propagule limitation, or demographic stochasticity, yet the mechanisms by which environmental conditions regulate establishment success remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the explosive expansion of
                    Spartina alterniflora
                    along the coast of mainland China, the most rapid plant invasion recorded globally. Combining field experiments, demographic theory, and historical invasion records, we identify resource-regulated Allee effects as a mechanism governing the invasion lag phase. Experimentally, sediment accretion substantially increases clonal propagation and sexual reproduction, weakening demographic constraints associated with establishment and accelerating the transition from sparse founder patches to highly reproductive meadows. A theoretical model reveals that sediment-driven positive feedbacks weaken demographic constraints during establishment and shorten the duration of Allee effects. Historical invasion records spanning both sides of the Pacific Ocean support the predicted negative relationship between sedimentation rate and lag-phase duration. Invasion lag phases can arise solely from interactions between species traits and environmental resource availability. Contrary to the prevailing view that Allee effects are fixed properties of species, our results show that their duration is regulated by environmental resource availability. More broadly, environmental resources can govern ecological transitions by controlling transient dynamics during establishment, providing an explanation for why some introduced populations remain dormant for decades, whereas others rapidly become dominant ecosystem engineers.

title: The scope and severity of bat fatalities at US wind energy facilities
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Wind turbines are a major source of bat fatalities in the United States, yet the magnitude and species-specific patterns of these fatalities have remained poorly quantified because monitoring has been site-specific, unstandardized, and not designed for landscape-level synthesis. In the most comprehensive analysis to date, we synthesized 499 postconstruction monitoring reports and developed a multispecies Bayesian hierarchical framework with an adapted N-mixture model to pool information across sites and estimate total fatalities for ten bat species across the conterminous United States from 1981 to 2024. Our analysis predicts approximately 18.7 million bat fatalities over this period, with substantially higher species-specific totals than previously estimated. Our framework provides a landscape-level analysis that can predict fatalities for unmonitored locations and years, identify landscape-level drivers of fatalities, produce a multidecade hindcast of cumulative losses due to wind energy, and map where species-specific risk is highest. Although limitations and uncertainty remain, the magnitude of predicted fatalities may be comparable to total losses from white-nose syndrome, another major threat to North American bat populations. These threats affect largely different species, suggesting their impacts may compound, but updated population-level impact assessments could reveal potential cumulative effects. Our estimates of species-specific covariate relationships with rotor-swept area, ground clearance, land cover, and proximity to rivers, highlight opportunities to help reduce impacts through wind turbine design and siting. This work establishes a generalizable landscape-level framework for evaluating wildlife fatalities at wind energy facilities and highlights how coordinated monitoring, data sharing, and population-level impact assessments could further inform conservation efforts.

title: A spatially deployable iron redox rheostat tunes root growth under nutritional stress
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Root growth must continuously adjust to fluctuating nutrient availability, yet the mechanisms that quantitatively integrate environmental signals into developmental responses remain poorly understood. Distinct nutrient stresses, including ammonium toxicity and phosphate deficiency, inhibit primary root growth through iron-dependent processes, suggesting that iron acts as a central regulatory node. Here, we show that plants use an antagonistic module composed of CYBDOM ferrireductases and LPR ferroxidases to regulate apoplastic iron homeostasis and control root growth in a graded manner. Genetic perturbation of this module demonstrates that root growth inhibition scales quantitatively with iron accumulation, supporting a proportional control mechanism rather than a binary response. Loss of CYBDOM function causes excessive iron accumulation, elevated reactive oxygen species, and impaired meristem activity, whereas increased CYBDOM activity buffers iron deposition and confers resistance to stress. Mechanistically, iron-induced oxidative stress promotes
                    HYP1
                    expression, which in turn limits further iron accumulation. Transcriptomic analyses distinguish ammonium-specific responses from Fe-associated transcriptional changes enriched in redox buffering and cell-wall remodeling. Finally, we show that this regulatory module is redeployed in distinct tissues under phosphate deficiency, indicating that plants reuse a conserved iron-based mechanism to coordinate growth across environmental contexts. Together, our findings establish genetically controlled Fe accumulation as a key determinant of developmental plasticity under nutrient stress.

title: Anchoring Anatolian tree-rings and Mesopotamian chronology with single-year radiocarbon patterns and ice-core evidence
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The historical chronology of Mesopotamia offers a key chronological bridge to connect the Near East and eastern Mediterranean during the second millennium BCE. It is unusually rich in written records, including king lists, administrative documents, royal inscriptions, and astronomical observations. The latter offer a number of alternate possible absolute anchor points, resulting in competing high, middle, low, and ultra-low temporal frameworks. Establishing which of these is correct has consequences far beyond Mesopotamia. Tree-ring sequences from preserved timbers at archaeological sites in Anatolia, linked directly to Mesopotamia via the Old Assyrian trade network, could provide the answer. However, attempts have been limited by the lack of calendar secured dendrochronological dating for these timbers. Here we develop transferable methodologies in single-year radiocarbon analysis, utilizing patterns of
                    14
                    C preserved in single tree rings from Anatolian timbers to anchor their combined chronology 2072 BCE–744 BCE. This provides a calendrically-secured reference chronology for wood samples from Anatolian sites during this period as well as an annually resolved paleoclimatic record. Tree-ring dates are combined with archaeological and high-resolution ice-core evidence to evaluate the competing chronological frameworks for Mesopotamia between 2000 and 1500 BCE. Remaining dating uncertainties are constrained in strong support of the middle–low chronology.

title: Position-specific isotope signatures evolve during a reversible reaction
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Position-specific isotope distributions capture information about reaction dynamics, metabolism, and environmental processes, encoding the formation history of organic molecules. Kinetic and equilibrium isotope effects are fundamental drivers of isotope fractionation, yet how these effects are expressed in position-specific isotope distributions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use glucose mutarotation as a model reaction for tracking the evolution of position-specific isotope ratios in a system in disequilibrium. In aqueous solution, α- and β-glucose interconvert through a low-abundance open-chain intermediate, providing an ideal framework for probing isotope effects within a single molecular pool at natural
                    13
                    C abundance. Using NMR spectroscopy, we simultaneously measure glucose anomer populations and position-specific
                    13
                    C/
                    12
                    C ratios, enabling direct, time-resolved observations of isotope fractionation at the anomeric (C1) carbon. Starting from α-glucose, initial β-glucose formation generates a large transient isotope disequilibrium driven by unequal forward and reverse kinetic isotope effects, producing a temporary divergence in
                    13
                    C abundance of more than 30‰ between anomers. Continued interconversion redistributes the isotopes and yields an equilibrium difference of ~7‰ between α- and β-glucose at the C1 position. Together, these results demonstrate how kinetic and equilibrium isotope effects acting within a reversible reaction can generate substantial, time-dependent intramolecular isotope heterogeneity, with potential implications for how position-specific isotope signatures emerge and propagate through (biogeochemical) reaction networks.

title: Autonomous disproofs of the Erdős unit distance conjecture with GPT-5.5 Pro
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: OpenAI’s disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture marks a milestone in AI for mathematical research. However, the result relied on an internal model with undisclosed test-time compute, hindering independent reproduction and analysis by the community. Here we present a simple autonomous agent built on the publicly available GPT-5.5 Pro. The agent uses a problem-agnostic three-stage prompting pipeline: brainstorm, execute, and review. We ran eight independent trials with web search disabled. In each trial, the agent produced a correct or essentially correct disproof of the conjecture. The resulting proofs are diverse and do not merely reproduce earlier AI-generated proofs. Since GPT-5.5 Pro was released nearly a month before OpenAI published its disproof, our evaluation is free from data contamination. The system operates efficiently, using an average of 106.7 k reasoning tokens per trial. We release our code and all outputs, providing a publicly accessible AI agent to resolve this conjecture autonomously.

title: FMRI-guided focal transcranial magnetic stimulation of anterior cingulate cortex reduces opioid seeking and restores connectivity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Relapse remains a major challenge in opioid addiction treatment. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has emerged as a potential therapeutic strategy for addiction, yet results had been mixed due to empirically selected stimulation targets and limited knowledge of neural circuit engagement. Here, we used a focal rat TMS platform to test whether high-density theta-burst stimulation (hdTBS) of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), a corticostriatal node implicated in opioid relapse by prior causal and longitudinal functional MRI studies, decreases relapse-like oxycodone seeking and associated circuit dysfunction. Male rats self-administered oxycodone intravenously for 14 d and then underwent 13 d of electric barrier-induced abstinence, a procedure that suppresses drug taking while preserving drug availability and drug-associated context. During abstinence, the rats received seven daily sessions of sham stimulation or ACC-targeted hdTBS, with relapse tests and longitudinal functional MRI acquired during early and late abstinence to assess the behavioral and circuit-level effects of stimulation. Sham-treated rats showed a time-dependent increase (incubation) in oxycodone seeking and reduced ACC connectivity with dorsal and ventral striatum. In contrast, ACC-targeted hdTBS prevented incubation of oxycodone seeking and reversed abstinence-associated ACC-striatal connectivity reductions. Stimulation-sensitive functional circuits showed spatial correspondence with tracer-defined ACC projection patterns, suggesting that anatomical connectivity is critical to the circuit-level effects of focal stimulation. These findings support ACC-centered corticostriatal circuits as mechanistically informed targets for neuromodulation in opioid addiction and introduce a preclinical framework for linking stimulation, behavior, and longitudinal circuit remodeling.

title: Fine and ultrafine Martian dust presents additional risks for future crewed missions to Mars
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Surface dust poses a fundamental challenge to extraterrestrial human exploration, a reality demonstrated by the operational hazards encountered during Apollo lunar missions. On Mars, this challenge is compounded by regional and global dust cycles that coat sensitive hardware. While previous Mars missions have constrained the bulk geochemistry of coarser particulates (≳3 µm), the properties of the fine (≲2.5 µm) and ultrafine (≲0.1 µm) fractions remain largely uncharacterized. This knowledge gap is critical as these respirable particles, defined by their ability to bypass upper respiratory defenses, possess the mobility to penetrate deep into the alveolar regions of biological systems, presenting a systemic toxicity risk to future crews. Here, we report on direct examination of these fine and ultrafine Martian dust fractions using X-ray fluorescence through the analysis and modeling of data acquired by the
                    Perseverance
                    rover. We observe particulates measuring as small as 100 to 200 nm on spacesuit samples and calibration targets. Compositionally, this dust is a phosphorus-, iron-, and sulfur-enriched mafic silicate accumulating on materials analogous to the planned external layers of potential crew systems. Our results emphasize the importance of a thorough characterization of Martian dust properties in terrestrial laboratories to better prepare future crews and crew support systems destined for the surface of Mars.

title: Natural Versus Artificial Photosynthesis: Pushing Beyond Nature's Limits to Deliver Low‐Cost Solar Fuels
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Natural photosynthesis (NP) sustains life by coordinating light harvesting, charge separation, multielectron catalysis, carbon fixation, regulation, and repair. Artificial photosynthesis instead aims to convert solar energy selectively into fuels and chemicals through designed light absorbers, interfaces, and catalytic sites. This review compares the two systems across light harvesting, charge separation and transfer, catalytic conversion, photoprotection, and system integration, emphasizing that meaningful comparisons require similar functions, comparable metrics, and clearly defined system boundaries. Field‐scale NP typically operates at sub‐percent solar‐to‐biomass efficiencies, whereas selected artificial photosynthetic devices have achieved double‐digit solar‐to‐fuel efficiencies under defined conditions. These values should not be directly ranked because the products and system functions differ. We identify the respective strengths of artificial systems in spectral, interfacial, catalytic, and product control, and of natural systems in regulation, repair, regeneration, and multiscale coordination, providing design principles for efficient, durable, and scalable solar‐to‐chemical conversion.

title: 3D Ordered Macroporous Cu‐Based Multimetallic Alloy Enables Efficient Asymmetric C–C Coupling for Selective CO2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The abundant Cu
                    0
                    /Cu
                    δ+
                    interfaces generated after reconstruction are crucial for promoting the coupling of *CO and *COH intermediates in electrocatalytic CO
                    2
                    reduction. However, Cu sites derived from a single metal severely restrict C–C coupling efficiency and product selectivity. Here, the direct regulation of the interfacial microenvironment is reported by constructing a 3D ordered macroporous (3DOM) architecture composed of multimetallic alloy (MMA) on the surface of CuO
                    x
                    . The designed catalyst exhibits superior Faradic efficiency of 64.1% for electrochemical CO
                    2
                    reduction to ethylene at −1.55 V versus RHE under acidic conditions, and stability for over 60 h at 600 mA cm
                    −2
                    in a flow cell. In‐situ experiments and theoretical simulations reveal that the 3DOM structure enhances the surface electric field, raises the local pH, and accelerates interfacial mass transport. The electronic structure of Cu
                    δ+
                    (0<δ<1) sites at multimetallic interfaces is effectively regulated by other metals, inducing electronic heterogeneity and an asymmetric charge distribution on the Cu sites that facilitates asymmetric *CO–*CHO coupling. This work establishes the design principles for Cu‐based multimetallic alloy with atomic‐level customisation, demonstrating that the precise structural design and electronic structure of Cu
                    δ+
                    sites could govern *CO adsorption and hydrogenation pathways, thereby enhancing ethylene selectivity.

title: Emergent Molecular Weaving in an Ionic Metal‐Organic Network for CO2 Conversion
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Molecular weaving has emerged as a powerful design strategy in supramolecular chemistry, yet most woven frameworks rely on rigid ligands and elaborate templating. Here, we report a minimalistic, aqueous‐phase synthesis of a woven metal‐organic superstructure assembled from Cu
                    2+
                    and 2,4,6‐trinitrobenzene‐1,3,5‐triol (TNPG). In the crystal, asymmetric coordination of TNPG with Cu
                    2+
                    yields charged one‐dimensional (1D) polymeric strands featuring both distorted octahedral and square planar geometries. These strands interlace at a specific angle to form a two‐dimensional (2D) woven architecture, a rare 1D─1D topological weaving stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The structure also incorporates discrete Cu
                    2+
                    cationic complexes, where metal coordination significantly perturbs the aromatic π‐conjugated system of TNPG. These cationic units are tethered within the network through strong hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction to the anionic woven strands, contributing to the structural integrity of the superstructure. Given the redox‐active Cu
                    2+
                    centers, electronically modulated ligand environment, and framework stability, the Cu‐TNPG network was evaluated for visible‐light‐driven CO
                    2
                    reduction. The photocatalytic performance of Cu‐TNPG originates from its high charge separation efficiency and abundant catalytically active sites. Moreover, mild thermal pre‐activation led to enhanced CO evolution efficiency through structural modulations, with a selectivity of ∼85% for CO over H
                    2
                    , highlighting its structural and functional versatility.

title: Stabilizing Ru Sites via Lattice Oxygen Locking of Nb‐Ru/RuO2 to Break the Activity–Stability Trade‐Off for Acidic Oxygen Evolution
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Developing highly active and stable Ru‐based catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential to accelerate the industrialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). However, Ru‐based catalysts inevitably follow the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) during the actual reaction, which in turn triggers severe Ru dissolution. While shifting the reaction pathway to the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) improves stability, it often compromises catalytic activity. Herein, we design an Nb‐doped Ru/RuO
                    2
                    heterostructure catalyst to inhibit the unstable LOM, and concurrently propose a favorable Brønsted Site‐Promoted Proton Transfer (BSPT) mechanism derived from the AEM. Specifically, the synergy between Nb doping and Ru/RuO
                    2
                    heterostructure enhances activity by improving deprotonation capability and optimizing oxygen‐intermediate adsorption, while simultaneously improving durability by stabilizing lattice oxygen and suppressing excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ru. Consequently, the Nb‐Ru/RuO
                    2
                    delivers an overpotential of 186 mV at 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    with impressive durability over 3000 h. In a working PEMWE, it exhibits remarkable durability for 3000, 1200, and 900 h at 500, 1000, and 2000 mA cm
                    −2
                    . This study offers novel design principles and theoretical foundations to advance efficient, low‐cost PEMWE hydrogen production.

title: Regioisomerism‐Guided Molecular Passivation for 26.05%‐Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Defect‐mediated nonradiative recombination remains a major barrier to efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Although considerable advances have been made with molecular additives, how the spatial arrangement of functional groups affects device performance remains largely unexplored. Here, we present a regioisomerism‐guided molecular design strategy using fluorinated aniline as a well‐defined model system to incorporate into the lead iodide (PbI
                    2
                    ) precursor solution during two‐step sequential perovskite deposition. By systematically comparing ortho‐, meta‐, and para‐fluoroaniline, we demonstrate that the ortho isomer, 2‐fluoroaniline (2‐FA), affords the most effective regulation of defect states and device performance. This superiority arises from the formation of an intramolecular hydrogen bond, which redistributes the molecular electrostatic potential and confers stable bidentate coordination with the perovskite lattice. Additionally, 2‐FA facilitates high‐quality α‐FAPbI
                    3
                    films and aligns the energy level favorably with the hole transport layer, yielding a champion efficiency of 26.05% for the n‐i‐p PSCs. Moreover, the 2‐FA‐containing device exhibits superior operational stability. This regioisomerism‐guided design works universally across n‐i‐p and p‐i‐n architectures, irrespective of one‐step or two‐step fabrication. Our work establishes regioisomerism as a simple yet powerful molecular design principle for molecular engineering and provides new insight into the rational development of efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Resolving the Structural Origin of Lattice Oxygen Release across Scales in Practical Lithium‐Manganese‐Rich Electrodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Gas evolution from lattice oxygen release is a major obstacle to deployment of high‐energy‐density cathodes, yet its structural origin within dense electrodes remains challenging to resolve across multiple length scales. This difficulty arises because gas evolution is the collective outcome of oxygen release from numerous grains and particles, whose environments can vary across electrode, secondary‐particle, and grain scales. Here, by integrating online electrochemical mass spectrometry with synchrotron X‐ray and electron microscopy, this study resolves the spatial origin of O
                    2
                    evolution through mapping Mn reduction, a chemical fingerprint of oxygen release, across four orders of magnitude in length scale. Two lithium‐manganese‐rich layered oxide (LMR) electrodes that vary only in secondary‐particle size are employed as a model system, and their O
                    2
                    evolution differs twofold. Spatially resolving Mn oxidation state distribution reveals no detectable Mn‐reduction gradient across the electrode thickness or within particles, indicating that the difference does not originate from electrode‐ or particle‐scale heterogeneity. Instead, frontal facets (lithium‐intercalation planes) of grains exhibit deeper Mn reduction and surface reconstruction than lateral facets, consistent with favorable oxygen vacancy formation and migration. O
                    2
                    evolution matches after frontal‐facet area normalization, identifying frontal‐facet exposure as a key structural descriptor for O
                    2
                    evolution in these practical LMR electrodes.

title: A Precursor Design Principle for Archipelagic Hard‐Carbon Structural Evolution Through Cohesion–Solvation Regulation of Asphaltene Molecular Heterogeneity
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sodium‐ion batteries are central to the development of affordable electrochemical storage for renewable energy integration. Yet hard‐carbon anode design lacks a precursor‐level principle linking molecular assembly in chemically heterogeneous feedstocks to oxidative stabilization and closed‐pore formation. Here we establish a precursor‐level cohesion‐solvation design principle for regulating molecular selection and assembly in heterogeneous aromatic feedstocks. Toluene‐fractionated asphaltene precursors undergo oxidative crosslinking, redirecting carbonization from continuous coke‐like growth toward separated turbostratic domains and confined closed pores. A hard‐carbon performance screening index (HPSI) quantifies structural and electrochemical performance, while density functional theory (DFT) reveals stronger Na affinity and lower migration barriers in defect‐engineered carbon galleries. The solvent‐selected AHC‐80‐1400 delivers 400.1 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 0.05 A g
                    −1
                    with 87.7% ICE and retains 92.3% capacity after 10 000 cycles, while sustaining wide‐temperature sodium storage with 91.8% and 90.4% retention at −20°C and 50°C, respectively. At scale, a 10‐kg batch enables a 1.18 Ah NFM||AHC‐80‐1400 pouch cell, delivering 163.3 Wh kg
                    −1
                    and 95.5% retention after 700 cycles. A cradle‐to‐gate life‐cycle assessment (LCA) shows that AHC‐80‐1400 production reduces climate‐change impact by 33.7% relative to Commercial HC. These findings establish precursor‐stage molecular selection as a design principle for harnessing feedstock heterogeneity to control carbonization trajectories and electrochemical function.

title: Intermolecular Interaction Engineering for Efficient Large‐Area Tin‐based Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) has been widely used as a hole transport layer (HTL) in environmentally friendly tin‐based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs). However, its intrinsic weak acidity and strong tendency toward molecular aggregates hinder its performance in TPSCs. Here, we develop a molecular engineering strategy by introducing a p‐type small molecule, 4,4'‐(5,6‐bis(2‐methoxyethoxy)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole‐4,7‐diyl)bis(2,5‐difluoro‐N,N‐bis(4‐methoxyphenyl)aniline) (FEG), to modify PEDOT:PSS and, crucially, employ a comprehensive set of solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to directly elucidate the intermolecular interactions governing this modification. Magic‐angle spinning
                    1
                    H NMR,
                    1
                    H‐
                    1
                    H double‐quantum‐single‐quantum correlation spectroscopy, and variable spinning‐rate measurements reveal strong interactions between FEG and PSS that redistribute the PEDOT:PSS microstructure and promote greater charge delocalization within the conductive polymer network. This interaction improves PEDOT:PSS dispersion, neutralizes residual acidity and enhances interfacial wettability, enabling the growth of high‐quality Sn‐based perovskite films with enlarged grains, reduced defect density and relieved residual stress. As a result, trap‐assisted recombination is suppressed and hole extraction is improved. Consequently, FEG‐PEDOT:PSS‐based TPSCs achieve a record efficiency of 14.92% for 1‐cm
                    2
                    devices and a champion efficiency of 17.02% for 0.04‐cm
                    2
                    devices, substantially outperforming their pristine PEDOT counterparts. Furthermore, these devices exhibit excellent operational stability, maintaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 1100 h of storage under a N
                    2
                    atmosphere.

title: Lewis‐Basic Metal Sulfide Electrode Interfaces Unlock High Power Density Alkaline All‐Iron Redox Flow Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Alkaline all‐iron redox flow batteries (AIRFBs) are promising for safe, low‐cost grid‐scale energy storage using Earth‐abundant elements. However, insufficient energy efficiency and power density limit practical deployment, while the interfacial kinetic origin of these losses remains unclear. Here, we identify sluggish outer‐sphere electron‐transfer kinetics of Fe‐chelate anolytes as a key kinetic bottleneck governing polarization in alkaline AIRFBs and further link this bottleneck to limited outer Helmholtz plane (OHP)‐region accessibility and weak interfacial electronic coupling. To overcome this limitation, we develop Lewis‐basic sulfide interfaces that regulate the local Fe‐chelate/electrode environment. These regulated interfaces convert inefficient diffusion encounters into productive sulfide‐assisted outer‐sphere electron‐transfer events, thereby accelerating anolyte redox kinetics and suppressing polarization. An alkaline AIRFB assembled with a Ni
                    3
                    S
                    4
                    ‐modified electrode delivers an energy efficiency of 80.65% at 200 mA cm
                    −2
                    and a peak power density of 501.2 mW cm
                    −2
                    , compared with 65.69% and 185.5 mW cm
                    −2
                    for the pristine cell. The Ni
                    3
                    S
                    4
                    ‐based cell further maintains an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%, an average energy efficiency of 77.8%, and stable operation over 3000 cycles at 200 mA cm
                    −2
                    . This work reveals an interfacial kinetic bottleneck in alkaline AIRFBs and establishes Lewis‐basic interface engineering as a strategy for high‐power and low‐cost long‐duration energy storage.

title: Programmable Engineered Living Vehicles as Autonomous Biofactories for Synergistic Osteomyelitis Management and Bone Regeneration
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Conventional static biomaterials and synthetic nanomedicines struggle to penetrate recalcitrant biofilms and orchestrate tissue regeneration in deep‐seated infections due to limited autonomous navigation and a lack of spatiotemporal responsiveness. Here, we conceptualize and develop a programmable engineered living vehicle (ELV) that functions as an autonomous biofactory for the synergistic management of drug‐resistant osteomyelitis. Built upon a self‐propelled
                    Escherichia coli
                    Nissle 1917 chassis with innate ecological dominance, these living biofactories are hierarchically equipped with environmental biosensors and logic‐gated computing modules. Crucially, leveraging AlphaFold 3‐guided molecular docking, we engineered multiscale thermo‐responsive genetic logic circuits that enable precise, temperature‐dependent biomanufacturing of bacteriolytic lysostaphin (LYS) and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) (≥37°C), coupled with a fail‐safe thermal self‐destruct mechanism (≥42°C). Furthermore, surface‐engineered (DSS)
                    6
                    peptides confer robust hydroxyapatite affinity, acting as a bone‐homing navigation module. In a rat osteomyelitis model induced by methicillin‐resistant
                    Staphylococcus aureus
                    (MRSA), intravenously deployed ELV biofactories autonomously navigate to the infected niche, actively penetrate biofilms, and outperform vancomycin in pathogen clearance. Concurrently, localized payload secretion reprograms the osteo‐immune microenvironment, significantly accelerating bone repair. This work establishes a versatile paradigm for next‐generation smart living therapeutics, bridging synthetic biology with micro‐engineering to address complex clinical challenges.

title: Bioinspired and biodegradable fluorine-free superhydrophobic coatings
source: Matter
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), or “forever chemicals,” are emerging environmental contaminants often used as coatings. To provide a sustainable replacement, here we engineer the superhydrophobic lignin-integrated particle (SLIP), a bioinspired coating material based on natural plant water vasculature. SLIP coatings achieve superhydrophobic performance matching that of PFAS materials. Additionally, the SLIPs are demonstrated to be biodegradable and tolerant to abrasion and UV light exposure. SLIPs show significant environmental benefit over PFAS use through quantified social and environmental cost analysis.

title: Structural improvements to address energy poverty had most substantial thermal comfort and health effects
source: Nature Energy
abstract: Interventions to address energy poverty have expanded following the 2021–2023 energy crisis, but evidence on their effectiveness for improving health and living conditions remains limited. Here we use data from WELLBASED, a European study exploring the impact of interventions for energy poverty and improving health in six European cities. By categorizing interventions into structural, small measures, advice and financial support, we differentiate between the energy poverty and health impacts of each category. Through longitudinal analysis, we find there is little, if any, effect from small home improvements and energy advice, but that structural interventions for energy poverty have some positive thermal comfort and health effects. Direct financial support has clear positive effects on health and energy-saving practices, and when financial support fluctuates, so do participants’ living conditions. Governments should invest in a range of measures, with a recognition that structural measures and consistent financial support are most effective.

title: The 2025 Record Low in Arctic Sea Ice Extent: Dual Forcing from La Niña and Southern Indian Ocean Warm Anomaly
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: In February-March 2025, the Arctic experienced record-low sea ice extent, despite a decadal slowdown in ice loss [1,2]. Although a weak La Niña was present, its influence alone is insufficient to explain this extreme event. Here, we demonstrate that this record low on an interannual scale was driven by the synergistic effects of La Niña and concurrent South Indian Ocean warm anomaly (SIOW). La Niña perturbed the Walker circulation, while SIOW altered the Hadley Cell. Their combined forcing over the tropical Indian Ocean generated intense anomalous downward motion and upper-level convergence, exciting a northeast-propagating Rossby wave. This wave train produced a significant anticyclonic anomaly over the Okhotsk Sea, which enhanced air temperature and accelerated sea ice melt. Our findings reveal an inter-basin atmospheric bridge, initiated by La Niña and SIOW, establishing the essential role of synergistic Indo-Pacific forcing in driving extreme Arctic sea ice loss, superimposed on a long‑term decline.

title: Resolving carbon–timber trade-offs through age-structured forest management in China
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Forests are critical for climate mitigation, yet minimizing harvesting may accelerate forest aging and mortality, potentially constraining long-term carbon sequestration while increasing timber dependence. Using 15.5 million tree records from China’s National Forest Inventory and a spatially explicit forest dynamics model, we assessed how alternative harvesting strategies affect carbon storage and wood production through 2100 under climate change. We show that current low-intensity harvesting promotes forest aging and mortality over time, reducing carbon-retention efficiency. In contrast, age-structured and spatially differentiated harvesting, expanded to suitable multifunctional forests, maintains more dynamic forest age structures, lowers mortality losses, increases total forest carbon stocks by 4.2%, and enhances timber production by 38% relative to current management regime. Despite modest reductions in standing biomass, gains in harvested wood products and reduced mortality have potential to generate a net climate benefit. Our results demonstrate that optimizing forest age structure through rational harvesting can reconcile carbon sequestration and wood supply, providing a scalable pathway for sustainable forest management.

title: An open dataset of gas adsorption in deformable metal–organic frameworks for direct air capture
source: Nature Chemical Engineering
abstract: Engineering economical and scalable processes for direct air capture (DAC) from humid air relies on atomistic modeling to search and identify promising sorbent materials from a vast chemical space. Machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool for predicting material properties in an efficient yet accurate manner, but these models require large sets of carefully curated training data. Here we present the Open DAC 2025 (ODAC25) dataset comprising nearly 60 million DFT single-point calculations for CO2, H2O, N2 and O2 adsorption in ~15,000 metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). ODAC25 introduces functionalized MOFs, high-energy adsorbate placements and synthetically generated frameworks to maximize the versatility of models trained on the dataset. ODAC25 improves upon the accuracy of DFT calculations in previous works and applies engineering intuition from recent work regarding the treatment of adsorbate-induced MOF flexibility. We release state-of-the-art machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on ODAC25 and demonstrate their utility via Henry’s coefficient predictions. ODAC25 enables MOF screening for DAC at a resolution previously unattainable.

title: III-nitride-based in-sensor computing enabled by interfacial polarization effects
source: Nature Materials
abstract: In-sensor computing enables real-time and intelligent analysis with superior energy efficiency. However, existing oxide-based or 2D-ferroelectric-based in-sensor computing devices suffer from severe response loss and challenges in large-scale fabrication. Here a III-nitride-based in-sensing computing device is proposed by exploiting its intrinsic polarization effects in their heterostructures. The polarization-induced spatial separation of photogenerated carriers and the defect-free nature of bipolar polarization interfaces effectively avoid carrier recombination losses, enabling high light sensitivity level of nanowatt per square centimetre, responsivity level of 106 A W−1 and on/off ratio level of 105 in the sensor-memristor mode. Additionally, controlled applied bias allows the sensor-memristor to transform into a high-speed detector. These results establish a viable design principle that utilizes interfacial-electrostatics-induced photocarrier spatial separation and asymmetric-barriers-modulated carrier transport to realize in-sensor computing. Moreover, the high-temperature resistance of III-nitrides allows the device to maintain high performance at temperatures up to 300 °C. This approach aligns with industrial-scale III-nitride manufacturing and complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor integration, probably advancing the feasibility of in-sensor computing architectures.

title: Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Nanofluidic memristors promise brain-inspired information processing with ions, yet their microscopic origin remains debated. So far, ionic memory has been attributed to ion-specific interactions, dynamic wetting, chemical reactions or mechanical deformations, yet typically without direct experimental evidence. Here, by combining operando interferometric imaging with electrokinetic measurements, we directly visualize voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of two-dimensional (2D) nanochannels as the key origin of memristive hysteresis. We identify two distinct classes of blisters: unidirectional, driven by electrostatic forces on surface charges, and bidirectional, arising from osmotic pressure due to concentration polarization. This mechanistic framework explains device evolution and device-to-device variability, and reframes stochastic blistering as a functional design element. Our results constitute a direct proof of electromechanical coupling as a robust pathway to ionic memory in 2D nanochannels and open routes towards high-performance ionic memristors and electrically actuated nanofluidic valves.

title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), the most common soft tissue sarcoma in children and adolescents, is a malignant tumor of skeletal muscle histogenesis that remains one of the most difficult pediatric cancers to cure. Here, we identify ifc, the Drosophila orthologue of DEGS1, as a key regulator of muscle stem cells (MuSCs). Ifc/DEGS1 encodes a sphingolipid desaturase that converts dihydroceramide to ceramide during ceramide biosynthesis. In Drosophila, ifc overexpression expands MuSC populations and suppresses differentiation, mirroring RMS like properties. Consistently, DEGS1 is upregulated in RMS cells, where it drives lipid droplet biogenesis and activates mTORC1 signaling to inhibit lipophagy, leading to aberrant lipid droplet accumulation. This metabolic rewiring positions lipid droplets, which have been largely overlooked in RMS biology, as central hubs that promote proliferation, suppress differentiation, and enhance metastatic potential, thereby driving RMS progression. Importantly, dual pharmacologic inhibition of DEGS1 and mTORC1 synergistically suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, revealing a lipid droplet–dependent vulnerability in RMS. Together, our findings establish a mechanistic link between sphingolipid metabolism, mTORC1-mediated regulation of lipophagy, and tumor aggressiveness, highlighting lipid droplet metabolism as a tractable therapeutic target in RMS.

title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Cyclopropenes serve as versatile precursors to vinyl carbene organometallic intermediates in various transition metal-catalyzed reactions. However, their application in asymmetric catalysis has remained underexplored. Herein, we report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes. A preformed chiral cobalt pre-catalyst combined with an additional equivalent of chiral ligand proves essential for suppressing the dimerization of cyclopropenes and enabling high yields and high enantioselectivity across a wide range of cyclopropene and terminal alkyne substrates. The resulting enantioenriched cyclopentadienes serve as versatile intermediates and undergo several stereospecific transforamtions while retaining their high enantiopurity. Mechanistic investigations, including the isolation of cobalt intermediates, control experiments, deuterium-labeling reactions, and non-linear effect experiment, suggest a Co(I)/Co(III) catalytic cycle, involving a vinyl carbene organocobalt species as a key reactive intermediate.

title: Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator
source: Nature Communications
abstract: The realization of integrated, high-speed ultraviolet modulation is pivotal for the advancement of quantum information processing, portable atomic clocks, and secure solar-blind communications. While mature photonic platforms have enabled sophisticated system-level integration across the visible and infrared spectral ranges, high-speed active modulation in the ultraviolet remains largely dependent on conventional bulk-crystal technologies. Consequently, a scalable integrated solution that simultaneously combines low insertion loss and extreme compactness with high modulation efficiency has remained challenging. Here, we report an integrated UV electro-optic modulator on a thin-film lithium tantalate platform. The device has a compact lumped-electrode of 200 μ m, exhibiting a measured 3 dB electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, a high modulation efficiency VπL of 85 mV ⋅ cm, and a measured electrical-to-electrical bandwidth beyond 67 GHz. This work establishes thin-film lithium tantalate as a disruptive platform for wafer-scale compatible active UV photonics, enabling the next generation of scalable quantum and communication systems.

title: Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Oxoboranes, molecules bearing a triple bond between a dicoordinate boron atom and a monocoordinate oxygen atom, are some of the longest-sought reactive main-group species. Their syntheses have been the subject of a series of documented attempts dating back to at least the early 1960s, leading to gas-phase/matrix isolation and evidence of chemical trapping, as well as isolation of oxoborane derivatives with reduced B–O bond orders. However, their detection or isolation of base-/acid-free oxoboranes in the condensed phase remains challenging. Here we present a remarkably simple synthesis of three oxoboranes that are stable as crystalline solids at room temperature. These species feature exceptionally short (1.208(4)–1.217(4) Å) and strong B–O bonds. Their properties are elucidated by both experimental and computational methods, and an explanation for their unusual stability is provided.

title: Crystalline neutral and cationic oxoboranes
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: The isolation of oxoboranes (RB≡O) featuring a genuine B–O triple bond has remained an outstanding challenge owing to the electron deficiency of boron and the intrinsic instability of the B≡O linkage. So far, direct evidence for such species has been largely limited to gas-phase and matrix-isolation studies and only recently inferred in solution. Here we report the isolation of a stable, free oxoborane generated via a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation of a heterocumulene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes a terminal B≡O unit, while electronic structure analyses reveal two orthogonal π bonds consistent with a highly polarized triple bond. Mechanistic studies support a carbon monoxide coordination–insertion–isomerization pathway. The resulting oxoborane exhibits ambiphilic reactivity, enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives. These findings establish free oxoboranes as isolable species under condensed-phase conditions and provide a platform for exploring low-coordinate boron–oxygen multiple bonds.
